note: Fifty lock lines read by a person, one at a time, and labelled by hand. SAMPLE A (30) was read FIRST and the classifier's rules were written while looking at it, so agreement on A is optimistic by construction and is printed only for comparison. SAMPLE B (20) was read AFTER the rules were finished and never used to change them. B is the honest number and B is the one the gate holds. Sampling is deterministic: every lock line in laws/ sorted by the sha1 of its file and line, A is the first thirty and B the next twenty, so the sample cannot be quietly reshuffled into a flattering one. SAMPLE C (20 more) was read after sample B had already been used to FIX the rules, which contaminated B: 100% on B is a number the rules were repaired into. C is the only clean one left and C is what the record leads with. That is the whole reason three samples exist instead of one.

labels.ORDINARY: the ordinary English word: a locked door, a locked camera, a beat-locked scrub
labels.MENTION: the line talks about locking without declaring one: not yet locked, why it locked, the locked canon

PLAYABLE_SIDE_QUESTS:60 'THE LOCKED CRAFT RULES (baked in, gate-enforced)' was hand-called MARKER: it titles a block of locks. The machine calls it MENTION because 'the locked <noun>' is how this repo refers to locks that already happened. A known and accepted miss.

ANIMATION_AND_RAGDOLL:6 '**[LOCKED]** = decided, build to it.' was hand-called MENTION: it is the file's LEGEND explaining the tag, not a lock. The machine sees a bracket tag and calls it MARKER. The second known miss, and both are in sample C on purpose -- they are what the held-out number is for.
